title: A Soft Robot Tactile Finger Using Oxidation-Reduction Graphene–Polyurethane Conductive Sponge
authors: Hangze Li, Chaolin Ma, Jinmiao Chen, Haojie Wang, Xiao Chen, Zhijing Li, Youzhi Zhang
industry: 具身智能 / 柔性触觉
provenance: Primary publication and archived native research receipts. Internal receipts are not distributed with this release; hashes identify those records.
conditions: Figure 1 idealized prespecified 10 mm and 5 mm upper electrode heights
Independent bench performance tests on physical fingertip
model_chain: Prescribed compressed/uncompressed geometry to electrostatic capacitance
Separate benchmark pressure and grip tests
required_inputs: Electrode geometry and true contact area
Compression and contact test data for load inversion
limitations: Obtain both 3D top-electrode configurations or sufficient reconstruction parameters, measured contact area and matched dielectric properties.
Obtain compression/contact data and hold out paired displacement, force and capacitance for load prediction.
Bench pressure sensitivity, hysteresis, response time and force inversion require measured calibration and validation; the bench sample dimensions differ from Figure 1.

observations.detail: 53.3 pF at 10 mm and 167.5 pF at 5 mm.
Separate physical-sample test peak reported sensitivity approximately 1.089 kPa⁻¹.

routes.gap: No independent load predictions were verified. Obtain a measured capacitance–load calibration and hold out paired load, displacement and capacitance.

reproduction.scope: Native prescribed-height electrostatics and bounded displacement-to-mesh transfer. Contact, pressure inference and full reproduction remain unverified.
